newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares soar, up 35% since start of year.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares soar, up 35% since start of year.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended gains on Monday, jumping 5.91 percent and traders said growth could continue for months due to tenacious demand for stocks in newly privatised companies.
The 10-share SBI index surged 87.46 points to 1,566.9. The index has risen 35.5 percent since the first trading day of the year.
"Listings of newly privatised companies, which seem to appear regularly this year, offer constant incentive to the market. The index could grow by 50 percent this year," one broker said.

Petrol trader Istrabenz and Drug company Krka, which are expected to attract spirited investor interest, will be listed on the over-the-counter market of the bourse before February 10, while petrol trader Petrol and brewery Pivovarna Union are among firms that are expected to follow later in the year.
Overall 17 shares rose, three fell and five were untraded. Market turnover jumped to 992.9 million tolars from 591.7 million.

"Foreign investors currently account for over 50 percent of daily turnover. Their assessment is that Slovenian companies are cheap compared to similar firms in eastern and western Europe," Zoran Spasenic, a trader at brokerage BPH said.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active share, surging 6.84 percent to 33,130 tolars on volume of 18,361 shares for total turnover of 602.8 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the biggest gainer, rebounding 15.62 percent to 7,920 tolars on volume of 200 shares.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 7.86 percent to 6,450 tolars on volume of 288 shares.
